source_text:
Ἐξαρωμεν οὖν τοῦτο ἐν τάχει καὶ προσπεσωμεν τῷ δεσπότῃ καὶ κλαύσωμεν ἱκετεύοντες αὐτόν, ὅπως ἵλεως γενόμενος ἐπικαταλλαγῇ ἡμῖν καὶ ἐπὶ τὴν σεμνὴν τῆς φιλαδελφίας ἡμῶν ἁγνὴν ἀγωγὴν ἀποκαταστήσῃ ἡμᾶς.
πύλη γὰρ δικαιοσύνης ἀνεῳγυῖα εἰς ζωὴν αὕτη, καθὼς γέγραπται: Ἀνοίξατέ μοι πύλας δικαιοσύνης, ἵνα εἰσελθὼν ἐν αὐταῖς ἐξομολογήσωμαι τῷ κυρίῳ.
αὕτη ἡ πύλη τοῦ κυρίου: δίκαιοι εἰσελεύσονται ἐν αὐτῇ.
πολλῶν οὖν πυλῶν ἀνεῳγυιῶν ἡ ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐν Χριστῷ, ἐν ᾗ μακάριοι πάντες οἱ εἰσελθόντες καὶ κατευθύνοντες τὴν πορείαν αὐτῶν ἐν ὁσιότητι καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ, ἀταράχως πάντα ἐπιτελοῦντες.
ἤτω τις πιστός, ἤτω δυνατὸς γνῶσιν ἐξειπεῖν, ἤτω σοφὸς ἐν διακρίσει λόγων, ἤτω ἁγνὸς ἐν ἔργοις.
τοσούτῳ γὰρ μᾶλλον ταπεινοφρονεῖν ὀφείλει, ὅσῳ δοκεῖ μᾶλλον μείζων εἶναι, καὶ ζητεῖν τὸ κοινωφελὲς πᾶσιν, καὶ μὴ τὸ ἑαυτοῦ.
thought_title: The Gate of Righteousness and the Call to Humility
orientation: The Roman church is urging the Corinthians to end their faction quickly by turning to God in repentance, and now grounds this appeal in the image of the open gate of righteousness from Psalm 117 LXX.
pass_a_gloss: Let us remove therefore this [thing] in haste and let us fall before the master and let us weep beseeching him, that having become merciful he may be reconciled to us and to the reverent of our brotherly-love pure conduct may restore us. A gate for of righteousness having been opened into life [is] this [one], just as it has been written: Open to me gates of righteousness, in order that having entered in them I may confess to the Lord. This [is] the gate of the Lord: righteous [ones] will enter in it. Of many therefore gates having been opened the in righteousness this [one] is the in Christ [one], in which blessed [are] all the having entered and directing the way of them in holiness and righteousness, without disturbance all [things] accomplishing. Let him be someone faithful, let him be powerful knowledge to speak out, let him be wise in discernment of words, let him be pure in works. For by so much more to be humble he owes, by how much he seems more greater to be, and to seek the common-beneficial [thing] for all, and not the [thing] of himself.

choices.why: The glossary bans 'brotherly love' for ἀγάπη; φιλαδελφία is a distinct compound but the sense here is the mutual love among believers, so a periphrastic rendering avoids the banned phrase while keeping the meaning.
The author consistently uses δεσπότης for God as sovereign lord; 'master' preserves the authority relation without importing a liturgical title.
ἀγωγή here means a way of life or manner of conduct, not a physical path; 'conduct' fits the ethical context of the Corinthian appeal.
διάκρισις is the act of distinguishing or judging; 'discerning words' keeps the verbal object explicit and matches the context of speech-related gifts.
The adverb describes the untroubled manner of the righteous; 'without disturbance' is literal and preserves the negative prefix.

pass_b_english: So let us remove this quickly and fall before the Lord. Let us weep and beg him to be merciful and be reconciled to us, and to restore us to the pure and reverent conduct of our love for one another.
For this is the gate of righteousness opened to life, as it is written: “Open to me the gates of righteousness, so that I may enter through them and confess to the Lord” (Psalm 118:19).
“This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it” (Psalm 118:20).

Many gates are open, but this one in righteousness is the one in Christ. Blessed are all who enter through it and direct their journey in holiness and righteousness, accomplishing everything without disturbance.
Let someone be faithful. Let someone be able to speak knowledge. Let someone be wise in discerning words. Let someone be pure in deeds.
For the more someone seems to be greater, the more he ought to be humble, and to seek what benefits everyone, not what benefits himself.

polish.changed: Clarified the speaker and flow by making the opening exhortation a direct call to action, kept each Scripture quotation clearly attributed, and smoothed the final two paragraphs so the progression from the gate of Christ to the call for humility reads naturally aloud.

notes.why: Frequent switching between 'Master' and 'Lord' for God may seem intentional but lacks consistency.
notes.fix: Standardize divine titles or explain the variation.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'humility' for ταπεινοφροσύνη; 'humble' is adjective not noun form required.
last_rejected.fix: the more he ought to practice humility
last_rejected.ruling: ταπεινοφρονεῖν is an infinitive verb 'to be humble'; 'humble' correctly renders it. No noun form is required here.

last_rejected.quote: so that I may enter through them and confess to the Lord
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα εἰσελθὼν ἐν αὐταῖς ἐξομολογήσωμαι τῷ κυρίῳ
last_rejected.why: In this Psalm quotation the verb means give thanks or praise, not confess sins to the Lord.
last_rejected.fix: so that I may enter through them and give thanks to the Lord
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξομολογήσωμαι τῷ κυρίῳ in Ps 118:19 is 'confess/give thanks'; 'confess' is within the normal range (LXX ἐξομολογέομαι), and a translation-level preference, not meaning loss.
